hero.sub: ESP32-C3 based, pocket-size, open-source e-paper book reader. The model below is generated from real placement data — the position, size and height of every part are read from the hardware/pcb/placement.csv file.
hero.title: Pocket Reader
note.fix: Correction. The first design had a 58 × 30 mm body. But the panel glass is 59.2 × 29.2 mm — it would never fit into a 58 mm case. The body was corrected to 62 × 32 mm: 62 − 59.2 = 2.8 mm, i.e. a 1.4 mm bezel margin on each side of the glass. This dimension is derived from the glass size in case.scad, not chosen freely.
note.pcb: This is a placement proposal, not a production-ready PCB. Traces are not routed; thermal and EMC optimisation has not been done. The real layout must be done in KiCad and pass DRC. The repository deliberately ships no Gerbers: 13 pin numbers are still awaiting verification from the datasheet.
note.verify: Verification. gen_placement.py --check checks that every part stays inside the board, that no two overlap, and that the placement holds exactly the same set of parts as gen_netlist.py. 64 parts, 0 overlaps.
page.desc: 3D model, PCB layout, schematic and exploded assembly drawing of the ESP32-C3 based pocket-size e-paper reader.
page.title: Pocket Reader — Device, PCB and Case Drawings
sec.data.lede: The 3D model on this page and the 2D technical drawings beside it read the same placement file. Two hand-maintained coordinate lists in separate places would inevitably drift apart; using a single source prevents that structurally.
sec.exploded.lede: Six layers from front to back and the 13 mm thickness chain.
sec.pcb.lede: The technical drawings below are generated from the hardware/pcb/placement.csv file. Each part's pad, silkscreen and courtyard are drawn at true size.
sec.sch.lede:
26 nets, power path in orange, signals in thin black, blue labels are the net names.
      All values are verified against the datasheet.
sec.thick.lede:
The 13 mm body was not an arbitrary choice — it follows from the sum of the layers
      below. If you change the panel or the battery, this table must be recalculated.
sec3d.lede: Drag the explode slider to separate the layers. Drag to rotate, use the wheel to zoom. Click a part and its name and value appear in the top-right. The dimensions are real: board 45 × 24 mm, glass 59.2 × 29.2 mm, cell 26 × 21 × 4.5 mm.
